verdict.rationale: Crossmint's documented model has the user approve spending before money moves. Agent cards require the user to authorize an order intent, verified with a card-network passkey ceremony, which locks a fixed amount, merchant and expiration. Agent wallets bind the agent's signer to a permission set the user signs off on (spend cap, counterparties, time window), enforced onchain and revocable. Agent checkouts let the user handle secure inputs and steer the agent. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration, and a documented step-up confirmation for unusually sensitive purchases within an active mandate (wallet delegation explicitly runs with no per-action user prompt).
